descriptionAr: About the team The Integrations Ecosystem org builds the drivers, SDKs, connectors and BI integrations that make ClickHouse feel native in any stack. The Language Clients team maintains the official clients for Python, JavaScript, Java, Go, Rust, C++ and C#, plus the ODBC, JDBC and ADBC drivers. We're small, senior and remote across North America and EMEA. The role We're looking for a product-minded engineer to own the ClickHouse .NET client. You'll decide what the client should do by talking to the developers who use it, reading the issues and the telemetry, and listening to the community. Then you'll build it, with deep .NET expertise, and measure whether it worked. Your scope is the SDK and what builds on it: ADO.NET , Dapper and Entity Framework Core users, and the tools and integrations that depend on your client. What you'll do Know who uses the client and what they're trying to do. Define what good looks like (time to first query, error clarity, adoption by key integrations), measure it, and let that drive the roadmap. Be the voice of ClickHouse for .NET developers. Speak at .NET conferences and meet-ups, and write the posts, tutorials and samples that developers and AI assistants find when they search for how to use ClickHouse from .NET (SEO and GEO). Answer questions where the community asks them. Own the .NET client and its ecosystem: the client, the EF Core provider and ORM integrations, NuGet releases and support. Evolve it without breaking the people who depend on it. Review and co-maintain other clients, and take part in cross-client decisions on types, errors and protocol features. Bring what .NET and Windows users need to the ODBC driver, since that's how many Windows and BI tools reach ClickHouse. If you write C++, contribute to it directly. Bring written proposals about where we invest next. You set direction rather than wait for it. Make the client enterprise-ready: TLS and certificate handling, authentication including Microsoft Entra ID, safe credential handling, signed and reproducible packages, and the audit and compliance questions large .NET shops ask before they adopt. Shape the client for agents as users: an API, docs and error messages an AI coding agent can use correctly on the first try. Extend our AI development platform, with new workflows for maintaining the clients: consistency checks across languages, issue triage, release checks. About you Product-minded. You decide what to build from user evidence, measure whether it worked, and can explain what you chose not to build. 5+ years in software, much of it on data-intensive systems: drivers, SDKs, data access, ingestion or analytics. Deep C# and .NET expertise: memory management, async and the TPL, Span and pooling, profiling and benchmarking. You reason about throughput and latency down to allocations and bytes on the wire, and you prove it with tests and benchmarks. Fluent in C#, and productive in at least one more of our client languages (Python, JavaScript, Java, Go, Rust, C++). You'll review and co-own across clients, not only .NET. You've built or substantially extended a library other engineers depend on, and shipped NuGet packages across .NET Framework and modern .NET. You treat breaking changes accordingly. Fluent in .NET data access ( ADO.NET , Dapper, EF Core) and at home in the wider .NET ecosystem: ASP.NET Core, Aspire, NuGet. Security-minded. You've shipped a library into enterprise environments and know what security, compliance and procurement teams look for in a dependency. Enthusiastic about working in public. You've given talks or written technical content, or you're keen to, and you see it as part of the job rather than a distraction from it. Thoughtful use of AI development tools, with the judgment to review what comes out. Clear writing. Most coordination happens in design docs, PRs and RFCs. Nice to have ClickHouse, especially its type system, or another OLAP engine. C++ and ODBC driver internals. Building or maintaining an ADO.NET or EF Core provider. Open-source contributions to .NET or data infrastructure. Experience designing SDKs, docs or error messages with AI coding agents as the consumer. Protocol or wire-format work on a database driver or network client. Learn more Introducing the (blazing fast!) native TCP client for .NET : zero-copy columnar reads, 1.5 to 2x faster than HTTP, over 99% fewer GC allocations (Oct 2026) What's new in the ClickHouse .NET Driver: the road from 1.0 to 1.3 (Aug 2026) Meet GroeneAI: our autonomous contributor to ClickHouse (Oct 2026) Building a .NET API Gateway with ClickHouse and Aspire (Jun 2026) The .NET client on GitHub and its documentation ClickHouse Workload for Microsoft Fabric, now in public preview (Sep 2026) Perks Flexible work environment - ClickHouse is a globally distributed company and remote-friendly. We currently operate in over 25 countries. Healthcare - Employer contributions towards your healthcare. Equity in the company - Every new eligible team member who joins our company receives equity. Time off - Flexible time off in the US, generous entitlement in other countries. A USD$500 Home office setup if you’re a remote employee. Global Gatherings – We believe in the power of in-person connection and offer opportunities to engage with colleagues at company-wide offsites. Culture - We All Shape It As part of a rapidly scaling start-up, you will be instrumental in shaping our culture. Are you interested in finding out more about our culture? Learn more about our values here . Check out our blog posts or follow us on LinkedIn to find out more about what’s happening at ClickHouse. Our current operating model is built around disciplined, cross-functional campaigns: moving from abstract persuasion to local proof, pairing policy expertise with real-world use cases, and working with trusted validators who can help communities understand, shape, and benefit from AI. The team works closely with colleagues across Global Affairs, Legal, Safety, Communications, Product, Research, and other functions to build relationships that are substantive, durable, and grounded in two-way learning. About the Role As the U.S. External Affairs Manager, you will lead a portfolio spanning civil rights partnerships and federal AI policy, working with team leads to shape and advance OpenAI's engagement with civil rights organizations, civil society groups, researchers, and community-based organizations. This role combines independent strategic ownership, policy judgment, and external representation to help shape the AI policy debate in the United States. This role is central to the team's partnership and outreach operating model. You will help identify priority stakeholders, design engagement strategies, and build the external relationships and feedback loops. The work is not about one-way education; it is about co-design, listening, product and policy learning, and creating concrete proof points that can strengthen public trust. Reporting to the External Affairs Lead, you will work across the U.S. Policy and Partnerships team and in close coordination with State and Local Policy, Federal Affairs, Communications, Safety, Legal, Product, and Research. OpenAI is evolving quickly as we release new research, products, and tools. Day-to-day work may include representing OpenAI at convenings, designing a stakeholder strategy around a fast-moving policy issue, organizing partner briefings, preparing product and policy explainers, supporting local proof-point campaigns, coordinating quarterly partner reviews, or translating feedback from civil society into actionable insights for internal teams. This role is based in Washington, DC and may require frequent travel to meet with key stakeholders. We offer relocation assistance to new employees. In This Role, You Will Develop and lead federal AI policy initiatives within your portfolio in partnership with Federal Affairs, connecting civil society priorities, community feedback, and practical use cases to OpenAI's policy positions and advocacy. Build and maintain trusted relationships with civil rights, civil society, research, community, education, accessibility and other stakeholder organizations relevant to OpenAI's U.S. policy priorities. Help execute a repeatable engagement operating model grounded in co-design, localized benefits, trusted validators, cross-functional planning, and regular partner reviews. Develop stakeholder maps, engagement plans, briefing materials, and follow-up systems for priority policy campaigns and rapid-response moments. Support federal and state engagement strategies by identifying credible third-party voices, local proof points, and community feedback that can inform policy positions and advocacy. Represent OpenAI in senior-level policy discussions and external convenings, and prepare executives and subject-matter experts for meetings, roundtables, and public events, in coordination with Federal Affairs and relevant internal leads. Translate complex AI product, safety, and policy topics into clear materials for external audiences, including standing content packs and deeper product briefings for technology policy stakeholders. Surface external concerns and opportunities related to data and trust, deepfakes, child safety, job displacement, energy costs, copyright, civil and human rights, mental health, and other areas of public concern. Coordinate closely with Global Affairs, Communications, Legal, Safety, Product, Research, and other internal teams to ensure stakeholder engagement is accurate, thoughtful, and useful to the business. Track relationship health, engagement outcomes, commitments, risks, and follow-ups so the team can operate with accountability and continuity. You Might Thrive In This Role If You Are deeply familiar with the civil society, civil rights, and technology policy landscape in the United States. Are an effective coalition builder who can earn trust with a wide range of stakeholders, including groups that may be skeptical of OpenAI or AI more broadly. Enjoy working in fast-moving, ambiguous environments where strategy, execution, and judgment all matter. Can move easily between external relationship-building and internal cross-functional coordination. Are comfortable translating technical and policy complexity into clear, useful materials for non-technical audiences. Have strong instincts for where public trust, policy risk, and product reality intersect. Are energized by the promise of AI while taking seriously its potential harms and uneven impacts. We’re looking for someone with: Established network and credibility with civil society, civil rights, research, community, and other stakeholder organizations, including groups representing underrepresented communities. Deep experience in technology policy, public policy, public affairs, civil society engagement, advocacy, campaigns, or a related field. Strong understanding of the federal, state, and local policy institutions, processes, and debates shaping AI governance in the United States. Demonstrated ability to design and execute stakeholder engagement strategies tied to concrete policy, partnership, or public trust objectives. Excellent communication, presentation, briefing, and interpersonal skills,

descriptionAr: We’re looking for a Go-To-Market Compensation Lead to build and scale the incentive compensation programs that support our revenue growth. You’ll lead compensation design in partnership with the Head of Revenue Operations and GTM and Finance leadership, translating business priorities into plans that are clear, motivating, and financially sound. You’ll own commission operations end to end, including our incentive compensation management (ICM) system. This is a hands-on leadership role for someone who can move from strategic recommendations to detailed execution, operate independently through ambiguity, and take extreme ownership of both the numbers and the employee experience. What you’ll do Lead compensation design: Partner with the Head of Revenue Operations and GTM and Finance leadership to develop and evolve incentive plans across GTM roles. Recommend performance measures, payout structures, accelerators, and crediting rules that align incentives with company goals. Model business impact: Build scenarios to assess compensation cost, earnings opportunities, and incentive alignment. Evaluate plan performance and recommend changes as our products, pricing, and go-to-market motion evolve. Own commission operations: Run the full commission cycle, from source-data validation and crediting through calculations, reconciliation, approvals, and payroll handoff. Deliver accurate, on-time payouts and resolve questions and disputes with clear, consistent reasoning. Own the ICM system: Lead system configuration, plan implementation, testing, administration, and ongoing improvements. Partner with systems and data teams to maintain reliable integrations and reduce manual work. Build scalable processes and controls: Establish documentation, approval workflows, and audit trails for plans, exceptions, and adjustments. Create consistent processes for new hires, role changes, departures, and territory or account changes. Make compensation understandable: Lead plan communications and enablement so employees and managers understand how incentives work. Be the trusted point of contact for compensation questions and complex edge cases. Partner with Finance: Provide reliable payout reporting, accrual inputs, forecasts, and variance analysis. Maintain visibility into compensation spend and proactively flag risks or discrepancies. What you bring Relevant experience: 4+ years of GTM compensation experience in SaaS or another high-growth industry, with meaningful ownership of both plan design and commission operations. Autonomy and extreme ownership: A track record of setting priorities, identifying gaps, making sound recommendations, and driving work to completion without close supervision. You surface risks early and stay accountable through resolution. Exceptional attention to detail: A rigorous approach to validating data, testing calculations, documenting decisions, and catching errors before they affect payouts. Hands-on systems expertise: Experience administering an ICM platform and working with the CRM, finance, and payroll data that feed commission processes. Strong analytical judgment: Advanced spreadsheet and financial modeling skills, with the ability to evaluate trade-offs and turn complex analysis into practical recommendations. Clear communication and partnership: The ability to influence senior stakeholders, explain complex compensation mechanics simply, and handle sensitive information with discretion. Tact and sound judgment: The ability to handle exception and clarification requests from Sales tactfully, balancing responsiveness with consistent application of compensation policies. You know when to resolve requests independently and when to escalate to senior leadership with clear context and a recommendation. AI perspective and drive: A strong perspective on how AI is changing traditional commissions and compensation plan processing, and a passion for putting that perspective into practice across the business while maintaining accuracy, transparency, and controls. Nice to have Evolving business models: Experience with consumption-based, usage-based, or hybrid subscription models. Systems implementation: Experience implementing or migrating an ICM platform and automating compensation workflows. Technical fluency: SQL or BI skills to investigate data issues and improve reporting.

descriptionAr: GitLab is the intelligent orchestration platform for DevSecOps. GitLab enables organizations to increase developer productivity, improve operational efficiency, reduce security and compliance risk, and accelerate digital transformation. More than 50 million registered users and more than 50% of the Fortune 100* trust GitLab to ship better, more secure software faster. The same principles built into our products are reflected in how our team works: we embrace AI as a core productivity multiplier, with all team members expected to incorporate AI into their daily workflows to drive efficiency, innovation, and impact. GitLab is where careers accelerate, innovation flourishes, and every voice is valued. Our high-performance culture is driven by our values and continuous knowledge exchange, enabling our team members to reach their full potential while collaborating with industry leaders to solve complex problems. Co-create the future with us as we build technology that transforms how the world develops software. * Fortune 500® is a registered trademark of Fortune Media IP Limited, used under license. Claim based on GitLab data. Fortune 100 refers to the top 20% ranked companies in the 2025 Fortune 500 list, published in June 2025. Fortune and Fortune Media IP Limited are not affiliated with, and do not endorse products or services of GitLab. An overview of this role As a Staff Software Engineer on GitLab's Authentication team, you'll be the technical lead for how every user, application, token, and automated agent proves who it is on GitLab.com, Self-Managed, and Dedicated. We're an OAuth 2.0 and OpenID Connect (OIDC) provider for millions of users. We also accept identity from enterprise identity providers through Security Assertion Markup Language (SAML) and Lightweight Directory Access Protocol (LDAP). Behind that sit more than ten token types and several session methods that grew inside the Ruby on Rails monolith. You'll help us move this work onto GATE, GitLab's new authentication and authorization platform. GATE exchanges external credentials for short-lived tokens at the edge through a Secure Token Service written in Go.You'll set our technical direction, lead the hardest protocol and migration work yourself, and help senior engineers own the rest. Our projects include: OAuth across Cells: Making OAuth clients, grants, and tokens work when users and organizations live in different cells Global identities: One user identity that works across organizations and cells Token consolidation: Reducing the number of token types and moving token issuance and validation out of the monolith Identity for artificial intelligence (AI) agents and workloads: OAuth for Model Context Protocol (MCP) clients, workload identity federation, and service identities with narrow scopes What you'll do Own the technical direction for authentication protocols at GitLab, including OAuth 2.0, OIDC, SAML, and token exchange, across the Rails monolith and GATE services. Write and drive design documents and architecture decision records (ADRs) for multi-quarter work, then break that work into increments that ship behind feature flags. Lead migrations that must not break existing customers: token formats, client and grant state, and session behavior on GitLab.com, Self-Managed, and Dedicated. Be hands-on in the most complex parts of the code, in Ruby on Rails and Go, and review the designs and merge requests of other engineers. Agree interface contracts with the GATE Core, GATE Infra, Authorization, and Tenant Scale (Cells and Organizations) teams, and keep them current as the architecture changes. Treat authentication as a security and availability boundary: threat-model new flows, add rate limits and abuse controls, and lead the technical response to authentication incidents. Mentor senior and intermediate engineers on the team and raise the protocol and security knowledge of the whole group. Work asynchronously with engineers in India, Europe, and the Americas, with most decisions made in writing. Take part in on-call or operational support where your team’s ownership model requires it. What you'll bring Significant experience building and running production authentication or identity systems at scale, with technical leadership across teams that moves unclear problems to written decisions and shipped code. Deep, hands-on knowledge of OAuth 2.0 and OIDC: authorization code with Proof Key for Code Exchange (PKCE), refresh token rotation, token exchange, client registration, scopes, and JSON Web Tokens (JWTs) with signing keys and key rotation. Working knowledge of SAML 2.0 single sign-on and enterprise identity integration (LDAP, System for Cross-domain Identity Management (SCIM), or similar). Strong production experience in Ruby on Rails or Go, willingness to work in both, and experience with careful refactors, feature-flagged rollouts, and backward-compatible migrations in large, long-lived codebases. A security mindset. You think about token theft, replay, revocation, and blast radius before you think about elegance. Experience with multi-tenant software as a service (SaaS) systems, including data isolation and performance under high request volume. Clear, concise written English and comfort working in an all-remote, asynchronous company. Optional experience: authentication libraries (Doorkeeper, Devise, or OmniAuth), passkeys or multi-factor authentication, workload identity, gateways or policy engines, AI agent authentication, or multi-region architectures. Contributions to identity standards or open source identity projects are also welcome. About the team The Authentication group is part of the Security Platform stage, alongside Authorization, GATE Core, GATE Infra, Secrets Manager, and other security teams. We own sign-in, single sign-on, OAuth, and personal and service tokens. Our work touches every GitLab customer, and much of it is on the critical path for Cells and for GitLab's AI agent platform.

descriptionAr: Who are we? Cohere is the leading security-first enterprise AI company. We build cutting-edge foundation AI models and end-to-end products that are designed to solve real-world business problems. We’re training and deploying frontier models for enterprises who are building AI systems. We believe that our work is instrumental to the widespread adoption of AI and we are looking for folks that want to be part of that. We obsess over what we build. Each one of us is responsible for contributing to increasing the capabilities of our models and the value they drive for our customers. Cohere is a team of researchers, engineers, designers, and more, who are all passionate about their craft. We are a global technology company headquartered in Toronto with key offices in London, New York City, San Francisco, Montreal, Paris, Berlin and Seoul. Join us! Role summary: The Managing Editor runs the operational engine of the editorial team. This role turns strategy and drafts into a functioning production pipeline across all content streams (thought leadership, developer content, customer stories, product marketing content, etc.). This person is most responsible for whether things ship on time and at a consistent bar. Core responsibilities: In conjunction with Editorial Content Director, own and maintain the master editorial calendar across all content streams, sequencing work so there is no competition for the same limited writing capacity Manage the brief-to-publish workflow: assigning work, setting deadlines, tracking status, unblocking bottlenecks Own the review/approval routing for each content type: legal and PR for thought leadership, engineering/DevRel sign-off for developer content, customer and legal approval for customer stories, product marketing alignment for product content Set and enforce production-level style and quality standards (distinct from the Content Strategist's audience/strategy standards) Manage relationships with freelancers, contractors, and cross-functional SME contributors who feed content into the pipeline Report to the Head of Editorial Content on throughput, capacity, and delivery risk Own and manage the 24-hour review in the blog tracker Run competitive and content-gap analysis to identify where the team's limited capacity should go Ensures style guide story alignment (with Content Editor contributing) Present editorial performance metrics to cross-functional stakeholders in conjunction with Editorial Director Partner with Growth Marketing on content positioning alignment Work with MarOps on attribution and any potential pipeline content Qualifications 8+ years of experience in editorial or content operations Experience running multi-stream or multi-format editorial pipelines (not just a single blog) Full-Time Employees at Cohere enjoy these Perks: A weekly lunch stipend of $75/£75 or equivalent in your local currency for lunch. Full health and dental benefits, including a separate budget for mental health. RRSP matching, 401K, Pension Scheme. 100% Parental Leave top-up for up to 6 months, for either parent. Annual enrichment benefits: Arts & culture, fitness/wellness, quality time, and a workspace improvement credit. Education & learning stipend for conferences, courses, and coaching. 6 weeks of paid vacation (30 working days!) Budget for traveling to other offices if you are remote, plus an annual company offsite. How and Where We Work: Cohere is remote-friendly, but we also have offices in Toronto, London, New York City, San Francisco, Montreal, Paris, Berlin and Seoul with more opening soon. For those in the office: a daily lunch program, plenty of snacks, and regular community and social events. For those not near an office: a co-working benefit so you can work alongside others in your city. Everyone receives a $500 home office stipend to set up your workspace properly. If any of the above doesn’t line up exactly with your experience, we still encourage you to apply. We strive to create an inclusive work environment for all; we welcome applicants from all backgrounds and are committed to providing equal opportunities. Should you require any accommodations during the recruitment process, please submit an Accommodations Request Form , and we will work together to meet your needs. We may use AI-enabled tools to screen and assess applicants against the criteria for this position. This helps our recruiters identify potentially qualified candidates, but it doesn't limit the applications our recruiters may review or consider. Beware of Scams: Cohere will never ask for payment or third-party services (e.g., CV writing) as part of our hiring process. All legitimate roles are listed on the Cohere careers page and LinkedIn only, with all communications from Cohere employees coming from an @cohere.com or @cw.cohere email alias. If jobs are viewed on other sites then please verify these through our official careers page.

descriptionAr: About the Team The Applied AI Architecture team is responsible for helping developers and enterprises safely and effectively deploy OpenAI technologies in production. We act as trusted technical advisors and thought partners for customers, working side by side with their teams to identify high-value use cases, design practical architectures, and move from prototype to durable deployment. Cybersecurity is one of the most urgent domains where AI can help. Security teams are under pressure to reason across code, logs, infrastructure, tickets, alerts, and vulnerability data faster than ever. As frontier models become more capable, organizations need deep technical guidance on how to evaluate, validate, and safely deploy AI systems in security-critical workflows. About the Role We are looking for a Cybersecurity Applied AI Architect to partner with customers and help them apply OpenAI models, APIs, Codex, and agentic workflows to real cybersecurity use cases. You will work with CISOs, security executives, application security leaders, SOC teams, security engineering teams, and hands-on practitioners to identify where AI can create measurable security outcomes. This is a customer-facing technical role for someone who can move fluidly between executive strategy, practitioner-level cyber depth, and hands-on solution design. You will help customers evaluate and deploy workflows such as secure code review, vulnerability triage, threat modeling, remediation, SOC and incident response workflows, detection engineering, cloud security, GRC automation, and security validation. You will collaborate closely with Sales, Solutions Engineering, Product, Engineering, Research, and Security to turn customer needs into safe deployment patterns, reusable field assets, and product feedback. In this role, you will: Deeply embed with strategic customers as the technical lead for AI-enabled cybersecurity workflows, serving as a trusted partner to both security executives and technical practitioners. Lead discovery across AppSec, DevSecOps, vulnerability management, SOC/IR, detection engineering, red team, cloud security, identity, and GRC automation use cases. Build and deliver customer-facing demos, prototypes, workshops, proofs of concept, and reference architectures using OpenAI APIs, Codex, agents, scripts, CLIs, GitHub workflows, CI/CD systems, logs, tickets, scanners, and common security tools. Scope pilots with clear success criteria, data requirements, workflow integrations, evaluation methods, security constraints, safety boundaries, and human approval points. Advise customers on safe implementation patterns, including tool and function calling, structured outputs, retrieval, sandboxing, data handling, guardrails, telemetry, auditability, and approval-gated side effects. Translate between CISO-level outcomes and practitioner-level implementation details so each audience understands value, risk, and practical next steps. Create reusable field assets such as demo narratives, playbooks, FAQs, objection handling, qualification guides, assessment templates, and competitive positioning. Validate, synthesize, and deliver high-signal feedback to Product, Engineering, Research, Security, and GTM teams based on recurring customer requirements, blockers, product gaps, and emerging cyber workflows. You might thrive in this role if you: Have 5+ years of technical consulting, solutions engineering, security architecture, cyber advisory, deployment engineering, professional services, or equivalent customer-facing technical experience. Bring strong cybersecurity domain expertise across one or more areas such as application security, cloud security, identity, vulnerability management, secure SDLC, incident response, detection engineering, threat intelligence, red teaming, or security architecture. Can communicate credibly with CISOs, CTOs, security executives, engineering leaders, and highly technical security practitioners. Have hands-on experience building prototypes or production systems with APIs, Python or JavaScript, agents, scripts, CLIs, GitHub workflows, CI/CD systems, logs, tickets, scanners, or other common security tooling. Understand how to design AI workflows with retrieval, structured outputs, tool use, evals, guardrails, telemetry, sandboxing, and human-in-the-loop review. Are comfortable scoping pilots from ambiguous customer pain, including success metrics, required data, workflow integrations, evaluation criteria, deployment assumptions, and decision gates. Have evidence-first security judgment: you validate findings, separate true positives from noise, document assumptions, and avoid overstating model or security claims. Own problems end-to-end, operate with high throughput across multiple concurrent customer projects, and know when to stay hands-on versus create reusable leverage for the broader field. Have a humble attitude, an eagerness to help colleagues, and a desire to do whatever it takes to make the team and our customers successful. The median Ramp customer saves 7.5% and grows revenue 16% in their first year – far in excess of businesses operating without Ramp. We believe every ambitious company deserves the same. If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it. About the Role Solutions Consultant, Post-Sales at Ramp partner with Account Management to deepen and expand relationships with existing Ramp customers. You'll act as the technical and financial subject matter expert across the customer lifecycle — running product demonstrations to expand customers onto new Ramp products, while bringing the depth needed to resolve complex ERP integrations, configuration challenges, and technical blockers. You'll collaborate closely with Account Managers to assess requirements, design scalable solutions, and ensure fast time-to-value as customers grow with Ramp. You will partner with Post-Sales teams to drive Product, Design and Engineering teams' roadmaps to evolve Ramp to better serve our customers at scale and offer increasingly higher value to the customers. This role requires strong technical skills — comfort with APIs, ERP systems, and integration architecture — paired with the communication ability to translate complexity into clear business value for finance and operations stakeholders. descriptionAr: GitLab is the intelligent orchestration platform for DevSecOps. GitLab enables organizations to increase developer productivity, improve operational efficiency, reduce security and compliance risk, and accelerate digital transformation. More than 50 million registered users and more than 50% of the Fortune 100* trust GitLab to ship better, more secure software faster. The same principles built into our products are reflected in how our team works: we embrace AI as a core productivity multiplier, with all team members expected to incorporate AI into their daily workflows to drive efficiency, innovation, and impact. GitLab is where careers accelerate, innovation flourishes, and every voice is valued. Our high-performance culture is driven by our values and continuous knowledge exchange, enabling our team members to reach their full potential while collaborating with industry leaders to solve complex problems. Co-create the future with us as we build technology that transforms how the world develops software. * Fortune 500® is a registered trademark of Fortune Media IP Limited, used under license. Claim based on GitLab data. Fortune 100 refers to the top 20% ranked companies in the 2025 Fortune 500 list, published in June 2025. Fortune and Fortune Media IP Limited are not affiliated with, and do not endorse products or services of GitLab. As a Manager, Customer Success , you will lead a North America-based team that helps customers realize value from GitLab through strong adoption, measurable outcomes, and trusted partnership. You will partner closely with both executive sponsors and day-to-day end users/practitioners to drive adoption and measurable outcomes. Reporting to the Director of Customer Success, , you will coach Customer Success Managers and Customer Success Architects to support account health across onboarding, adoption stages, executive business reviews, and renewals, while also improving how the team works. This is a people leadership role with broad scope: you will develop talent, strengthen customer relationships, and partner across Sales, Product, Engineering, and other teams so customers are supported through growth, change, and escalation. What you'll do Lead a team of Customer Success Managers and Customer Success Architects focused on customer adoption, account health, customer satisfaction, and advocacy. Coach team members through regular feedback, development support, and career growth conversations to strengthen knowledge, communication, and execution. Partner with the Director of Customer Success to define team goals, clarify responsibilities, and align priorities with company direction. Manage resource assignments, staffing levels, and hiring activity to support team coverage and customer needs. Develop senior-level relationships with customers and support the team in building trusted advisor partnerships. Collaborate with Sales, Product Management, Engineering, Professional Services, and other internal teams to create a consistent customer experience. Support customers during escalations by working with other leaders to coordinate clear, effective responses. Improve the processes and tools used by the team and oversee initiatives tied to objectives and key results. What you'll bring Experience leading customer-facing teams in software, technology, consulting, sales, or customer success environments. Ability to guide teams that drive software adoption and manage customer relationships across onboarding, adoption, business reviews, and renewals. Knowledge of software development lifecycle practices, related tools, and agile or DevOps ways of working. Familiarity with cloud or container technologies such as Kubernetes and Docker, application security concepts such as static application security testing (SAST) and dynamic application security testing (DAST), or cloud platforms such as Amazon Web Services (AWS), Google Cloud Platform (GCP), and Microsoft Azure. Skill in translating strategy into clear initiatives, coordinating execution, and tracking delivery across competing priorities. Capability to lead distributed teams across regions, cultures, and lines of business, while working effectively with senior executives and external stakeholders. Willingness to travel occasionally for customer meetings and team events, as needed. Strength in communication, coaching, feedback, delegation, planning, and process improvement. Warmth and care in your leadership approach—able to coach with empathy and build trust on a human level. Interest in candidates with transferable experience who can connect technical concepts to business value and collaborate well across functions. About the team On the Customer Success team, we are accountable for customer adoption, measurable outcomes, customer satisfaction, and building customer advocacy across GitLab. We also act as a key connection point between customers and the broader GitLab ecosystem, helping streamline collaboration with Product Management, Engineering, Sales, Professional Services, and other partners. In this role, you will manage a team in North America while collaborating asynchronously with stakeholders across regions, with a focus on helping customers succeed at scale and improving how the organization supports them. The base salary range for this role’s listed level is currently for residents of the United States only. This range is intended to reflect the role's base salary rate in locations throughout the US. Grade level and salary ranges are determined through interviews and a review of education, experience, knowledge, skills, abilities of the applicant, equity with other team members, alignment with market data, and geographic location. The base salary range does not include any bonuses, equity, or benefits. See more information on our benefits and equity . Sales roles are also eligible for incentive pay targeted at up to 100% of the offered base salary. United States Salary Range $124,80

descriptionAr: Who are we? Cohere is the leading security-first enterprise AI company. We build cutting-edge foundation AI models and end-to-end products that are designed to solve real-world business problems. We’re training and deploying frontier models for enterprises who are building AI systems. We believe that our work is instrumental to the widespread adoption of AI and we are looking for folks that want to be part of that. We obsess over what we build. Each one of us is responsible for contributing to increasing the capabilities of our models and the value they drive for our customers. Cohere is a team of researchers, engineers, designers, and more, who are all passionate about their craft. We are a global technology company headquartered in Toronto with key offices in London, New York City, San Francisco, Montreal, Paris, Berlin and Seoul. Join us! Why this role? At Cohere, we strive to continually improve our large language models. Academic research and real-world experience has demonstrated that high quality, diverse datasets can contribute as much to the performance and capabilities of LLMs as the underlying model architecture and training regimen. We at Cohere believe data will play a central role in accelerating the advancement of our already world-class language models. Data is therefore critical to our success. Our ability to acquire data that is accurate, relevant, and timely is key to our ability to improve the quality of our models. We strive to continuously improve our data acquisition processes and systems to ensure that we have the data we need to stay competitive and meet the needs of our customers. We run frequent experiments to learn more about the role of data for model quality, from data mixtures, to cleaning techniques, to quality control. Please Note : This is a 1-year contract position. As a Data Partnerships Coordinator, you will: Scout new data partnering opportunities and manage the process end-to-end, including outreach, discovery, requirements definition, contracting, data transfers and regular data updates; triage data feeds issues as they arise Partner with Modeling to manage the relationships and data requirements with external data scraping vendors Facilitate hand-off of newly acquired datasets to Modeling and Annotation Product manage novel data collection methods and applications as needed Always keep an eye towards scaling the function with bespoke processes and tools You may be a good fit if: You have more than 3 years of experience managing data vendor programs You've worked in a partnership-focused role at an AI-focused company, and have built relationships with AI data suppliers You're proficient in data analysis and data management You're energized by proactively seeking out new data sources and building long-term, trusting relationships with vendors You enjoy cross-functional collaboration and have partnered with Technical and Business teams You're resourceful and approach problem-solving creatively

This role requires strong technical skills — comfort with APIs, ERP systems, and integration architecture — paired with the communication ability to translate complexity into clear business value for finance and operations stakeholders. This role is focused on Commercial and Mid-Market customers, supporting high-growth companies with standardized financial workflows and core ERP integrations. descriptionAr: ABOUT THE TEAM Business Marketing helps knowledge workers, developers, and business decision-makers understand and adopt OpenAI’s products, supporting both self-serve growth and our managed sales team. Our creative work makes complex capabilities clear, grounded, and human as they move from the lab into businesses and everyday work. ABOUT THE ROLE We’re looking for a hands-on Launch Producer to build and run a repeatable, scalable creative production engine for Business Marketing launches, spanning new models, products, and capabilities, as well as solutions and use cases. You’ll help shape the right creative and video approach for each launch, then lead production from brief through delivery. Most launches center on owned and social channels, and leverage video as a primary medium to explain new products and capabilities. Our largest launches also shape broader brand marketing, requiring coordination with Integrated Marketing and Media. This role combines building the system with running the work. You should be equally comfortable improving a workflow, leading a shoot, and partnering with a motion designer. IN THIS ROLE, YOU WILL Lead launch intake and planning, aligning creative scope, resources, and timelines with launch priorities. Partner with Product Marketing, Integrated Marketing, creative leads, and subject-matter experts to translate launch goals, audiences, messaging, and technical capabilities into compelling briefs, scripts, demos, and customer stories. Produce videos at varying levels of fidelity, including demos, motion graphics, sizzle videos, explainers, and talking-head or testimonial videos featuring OpenAI talent and customers. Lead production end to end: budgets, schedules, resourcing, shoots, post-production, and delivery. Consolidate feedback and approvals, manage dependencies, and surface risks and decisions early so assets are ready to ship. Partner with Creative Operations to assemble and manage the right production team for each launch, drawing on your trusted bench of freelancers, agencies, and production partners alongside internal talent. Set clear scopes, expectations, and quality standards. Plan assets for owned and social distribution, including formats, cutdowns, and channel-specific adaptations. Coordinate usage rights, accessibility, quality control, and final delivery requirements with the relevant partners. Partner with Demand teams to translate launch strategy into demand-generation creative, informing briefs, asset needs, and cutdowns while those teams own demand execution. Coordinate with Integrated Marketing and Media on major launches with broader brand and paid-media implications. Build reusable workflows, templates, and production approaches. Use AI-enabled tools, post-launch learnings, and asset performance to improve speed, quality, and effectiveness without adding unnecessary process. YOU MIGHT THRIVE IN THIS ROLE IF YOU HAVE 12+ years in integrated creative production, digital production, program management, or a related field, with a proven track record of managing complex creative initiatives. A true operator’s mindset: you can build a reliable production system and keep multiple launches moving through it. Strong storytelling and creative judgment, with hands-on experience leading video shoots and working with motion designers, editors, and other production specialists. An established network of creative and production talent, and sound judgment about the right team, scope, and approach for each brief, budget, and timeline. Fluency in post-production and delivering assets across social, owned, and demand channels. Clear, proactive communication and a collaborative working style. You build trust across disciplines, make tradeoffs visible, and keep teams aligned through shifting priorities. A scrappy, resourceful approach and comfort with ambiguity and tight timelines. You know when a simple demo is enough and when a launch needs a more ambitious treatment. A portfolio demonstrating end-to-end production leadership across fast-turn and larger-scale work, with your specific contribution and outcomes clearly identified. Work Location: San Francisco About OpenAI OpenAI is an AI research and deployment company dedicated to ensuring that general-purpose artificial intelligence benefits all of humanity. We push the boundaries of the capabilities of AI systems and seek to safely deploy them to the world through our products. AI is an extremely powerful tool that must be created with safety and human needs at its core, and to achieve our mission, we must encompass and value the many different perspectives, voices, and experiences that form the full spectrum of humanity. We are an equal opportunity employer, and we do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, sex, sexual orientation, age, veteran status, disability, genetic information, or other applicable legally protected characteristic. For additional information, please see OpenAI’s Affirmative Action and Equal Employment Opportunity Policy Statement . Background checks for applicants will be administered in accordance with applicable law, and qualified applicants with arrest or conviction records will be considered for employment consistent with those laws, including the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance for Employers, and the California Fair Chance Act, for US-based candidates. About the Role Buying software and services is still slow and fragmented at most companies. Employees don't know how to request what they need, approvals stall across finance, legal, and security, purchase orders live in a separate system from the bills that pay them, and finance teams spend month-end matching it all together by hand. Ramp's Procurement team builds the system that connects every step of that process, from the first purchase request through sourcing, approvals, purchase orders, receiving, and matching bills and contracts back to what was ordered. Procurement sits upstream of payments and works closely with Bill Pay, Accounting, and ERP integrations, so the systems we build shape how money leaves a business long before a payment goes out. We're looking for a senior backend engineer to own a core part of that system. You'll take responsibility for a product area such as the purchase order lifecycle, PO and bill matching, PO coding and accruals, or supplier and ERP integrations, set its technical direction within the team, and keep it healthy as customers and complexity grow. You'll work closely with product, design, and data partners to turn enterprise purchasing workflows into software that is flexible, auditable, and simple to use. descriptionAr: About Sentry Software runs the world and the pace is faster than ever. Sentry helps developers fix errors and performance issues before users notice, so teams can spend less time firefighting and more time building. Trusted by 200,000+ organizations, Sentry is today’s application monitoring standard and our team is building its AI-native future. About the role Sentry is looking for an Enterprise Account Executive to join our sales team. We need a strong hunter/self-starter mindset with the ability to methodically expand existing accounts. As a member of our sales team, you'll join a fast-growth start-up and hit the ground running and help develop our sales strategy and playbook. We're looking for an individual with experience selling SaaS/B2B products, especially to developer organizations. If you're a seasoned sales professional who is excited to work in a high-volume environment while helping define key strategic and operational initiatives, we'd love to speak with you! In this role you will Manage and work all leads and opportunities in your territory. Build and manage a sales pipeline while growing successful, long-lasting relationships with influencers (devops leads, engineering managers, procurement professionals, executives, etc.) to meet revenue targets and company goals. Manage, track, and report all sales activities with Salesforce proficiency. Deliver great product demos, provide insightful technical answers, and recommend creative ways to get the most out of Sentry. Be the voice of the customer to the Sentry engineering/product teams. Own the strategic planning for each Flagship account, developing strategies to drive adoption and geographic expansion, mapping and building widespread relationships across our customer’s organization. You’ll love this job if you You are a builder who works autonomously and relishes responsibility. Take pride in working to increase customer growth and happiness by aligning impact with the customer’s expectations of value. Thrive in a product-driven highly technical, fast paced and growing organization. Get a charge out of making a measurable impact on Sentry’s growth. Own the strategic planning for each strategic account, developing strategies to drive adoption and expansion, mapping and building widespread relationships across the customer’s organization, and working to increase customer growth and happiness by aligning Sentry impact with the developer community expectations and value. Qualifications 7+ years of technology direct sales experience, with current experience selling SaaS. Bonus points if you have experience selling developer tools to development organizations. High technical aptitude and are able to understand and discuss a developer-focused infrastructure product. Proven track record of exceeding sales targets and cultivating long-lasting relationships with clients. Deep curiosity for the developer tool space. Results-driven, with a desire to hunt new business and ability to try new processes and iterate to scale a global sales engine. Strong analytical, critical thinking, and problem-solving skills. You are a team player and comfortable in a fast-paced growth environment. You love the challenge and desire a fast-paced, challenging, and exciting environment! The base salary range (or hourly wage range, if applicable) that Sentry reasonably expects to pay for this position is $270,000 OTE with variable compensation. A successful candidate’s actual base salary (or hourly wage) amount will be determined by a variety of relevant factors including, without limitation, the candidate’s work location, education, work and other relevant experience, skills, and job-related knowledge. A successful candidate will be eligible to participate in Sentry’s employee benefit plans/programs applicable to the candidate’s position (including incentive compensation, equity grants, paid time off, and group health insurance coverage). See Sentry Benefits for more details about the Company’s benefit plans/programs. Equal Opportunity at Sentry Sentry is committed to providing equal employment opportunities to its employees and candidates for employment regardless of race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, age, citizenship, marital status, disability, gender identity, veteran status, or other legally-protected characteristic. This commitment includes the provision of reasonable accommodations to employees and candidates for employment with physical or mental disabilities who require such accommodations in order to (a) perform the essential functions of their jobs, or (b) seek employment with Sentry. We strive to build a diverse team, with an inclusive culture where every teammate can thrive. Sentry is an open-source company because we believe that everyone, everywhere, should have the ability and tools to make great software. Software should be accessible. That starts with making our industry accessible. If you need assistance or an accommodation due to a disability, you may contact us at accommodations@sentry.io . Want to learn more about how Sentry handles applicant data? Get the details in our Applicant Privacy Policy .

descriptionAr: GitLab is the intelligent orchestration platform for DevSecOps. GitLab enables organizations to increase developer productivity, improve operational efficiency, reduce security and compliance risk, and accelerate digital transformation. More than 50 million registered users and more than 50% of the Fortune 100* trust GitLab to ship better, more secure software faster. The same principles built into our products are reflected in how our team works: we embrace AI as a core productivity multiplier, with all team members expected to incorporate AI into their daily workflows to drive efficiency, innovation, and impact. GitLab is where careers accelerate, innovation flourishes, and every voice is valued. Our high-performance culture is driven by our values and continuous knowledge exchange, enabling our team members to reach their full potential while collaborating with industry leaders to solve complex problems. Co-create the future with us as we build technology that transforms how the world develops software. * Fortune 500® is a registered trademark of Fortune Media IP Limited, used under license. Claim based on GitLab data. Fortune 100 refers to the top 20% ranked companies in the 2025 Fortune 500 list, published in June 2025. Fortune and Fortune Media IP Limited are not affiliated with, and do not endorse products or services of GitLab. An overview of this role As a Principal Revenue Strategist, you'll help shape how GitLab brings its products to market as artificial intelligence changes how software is built and bought. Reporting to the VP of Revenue Strategy, you'll be a senior individual contributor connecting market, product, and field insights to clear recommendations and changes in how we sell. You'll take on complex, open-ended go-to-market questions with limited context, working directly with executive partners across Sales, Finance, and Product to decide where to invest, how to reach customers, and what needs to change. What you'll do Shape revenue strategy across customer segmentation, sales coverage, sales motions, and investment priorities. Design multi-quarter changes in how we sell and monetize, defining the implications for the customer journey, metrics, roles, incentives, and operating model. Build agreement on the path forward and partner with Field Operations and Enablement on execution. Develop market and expansion strategies, prioritizing markets, defining go-to-market models and capacity needs, and identifying the operational dependencies of entering or scaling in new regions. Connect go-to-market strategy and Product by translating field and customer insights into product input, and product direction into commercial implications. Provide focused, commercially grounded input on pricing and packaging. Contribute strategic inputs to long-range planning, including total addressable market, sales capacity, productivity, and unit economics, while Field Operations and Finance retain ownership of annual planning, quota setting, and territory design. Build models, write decision memos, run analyses, and facilitate working sessions to turn recommendations into action with cross-functional partners. Advise senior leaders in Sales, Finance, and Product independently, distilling complex problems into clear recommendations with explicit assumptions and trade-offs. What you'll bring Experience owning complex go-to-market or revenue strategy work in a growing technology company, consulting, or a combination of both. Relevant experience and transferable skills matter more than a particular career path. Direct experience solving business-to-business software go-to-market problems, such as segmentation, coverage, pipeline and conversion, sales capacity and productivity, incentives, or pricing and packaging. A structured approach to testing assumptions and turning an unclear problem into a framework, a recommendation, and practical next steps. Strong commercial and analytical judgment, including the ability to build models and recognize when the evidence is sufficient to make a decision. The ability to work credibly with senior leaders, challenge decisions with evidence, and influence people without formal authority. A collaborative, hands-on approach that treats execution as part of strategy, not a handoff after the recommendation. Helpful, but not required: experience with usage-based or consumption models, international expansion, enterprise or platform sales, or a technical or scientific background. Interest in people management over time is welcome, but this is an individual contributor role. About the team The Revenue Strategy team tackles strategic questions about how GitLab reaches customers, sells, and monetizes its platform. You'll work with Sales, Finance, and Product leaders to connect strategy with commercial decisions, and with Field Operations and Enablement to put those decisions into practice. GitLab is an all-remote company with a public handbook and a transparent, low-ego culture. Our mission is to enable everyone to contribute to and co-create the software that powers our world. The base salary range for this role’s listed level is currently for residents of the United States only. This range is intended to reflect the role's base salary rate in locations throughout the US. Grade level and salary ranges are determined through interviews and a review of education, experience, knowledge, skills, abilities of the applicant, equity with other team members, alignment with market data, and geographic location. The base salary range does not include any bonuses, equity, or benefits. See more information on our benefits and equity . Sales roles are also eligible for incentive pay targeted at up to 100% of the offered base salary. descriptionAr: About the Team Security is at the foundation of OpenAI’s mission to ensure that artificial general intelligence benefits all of humanity. The Security team protects OpenAI’s technology, people, and products. We are technical in what we build but are operational in how we do our work, and are committed to supporting all products and research at OpenAI. Our Security team tenets include: prioritizing for impact, enabling researchers, preparing for future transformative technologies, and engaging a robust security culture. About the Role As an Incident Commander on Detection & Response, you’ll lead the response to complex security incidents affecting OpenAI’s intellectual property, customer data, and infrastructure. You’ll establish response priorities, coordinate technical work streams, drive containment and recovery decisions within agreed authority, and keep stakeholders informed as facts evolve. You’ll work with security and infrastructure teams across endpoints, identity, cloud, and compute environments, maintaining clear ownership and effective handoffs across time zones. Detection engineering knowledge is a supporting requirement: you’ll use telemetry and detection logic to assess evidence, identify visibility gaps, and guide improvements that make incident response more effective. In this role, you will: Run incident command from initial assessment through containment, recovery, and closure, establishing severity, scope, response objectives, and escalation needs. Assign work stream owners and coordinate investigation, containment, and recovery in parallel. Maintain a decision log and distinguish confirmed facts from assumptions. Drive timely containment and recovery decisions with the appropriate owners, weighing security risk, evidence preservation, and operational impact within agreed decision rights. Communicate incident status, impact, uncertainty, actions underway, and the next update to technical and nontechnical stakeholders. Manage cross-time-zone handoffs with explicit command ownership, current status, outstanding risks, pending decisions, and next actions. Improve response readiness through exercises, playbooks, and post-incident reviews; track agreed corrective actions with their owners. Partner with detection engineers to evaluate telemetry and detection quality, close incident-related visibility gaps, and prioritize practical response automation. You might thrive in this role if you: Have personally led complex security incidents as incident commander or an equivalent response lead, with clear examples of decisions, delegation, escalation, and outcomes. Make sound decisions with incomplete information and revise them as evidence changes, balancing containment urgency with operational impact. Coordinate responders across teams and time zones, resolve conflicting priorities, and maintain clear ownership during handoffs. Communicate calmly and precisely under pressure, including concise stakeholder updates and explicit statements of uncertainty. Have the security and infrastructure fundamentals to challenge investigation findings and assess containment and recovery options. Understand detection engineering, including telemetry coverage, detection logic, false positives and false negatives, and validation. Can query and interpret evidence to support response decisions. Turn incident lessons into practical improvements to readiness, playbooks, detection coverage, and response tooling. About OpenAI OpenAI is an AI research and deployment company dedicated to ensuring that general-purpose artificial intelligence benefits all of humanity. We push the boundaries of the capabilities of AI systems and seek to safely deploy them to the world through our products. AI is an extremely powerful tool that must be created with safety and human needs at its core, and to achieve our mission, we must encompass and value the many different perspectives, voices, and experiences that form the full spectrum of humanity. We are an equal opportunity employer, and we do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, sex, sexual orientation, age, veteran status, disability, genetic information, or other applicable legally protected characteristic. For additional information, please see OpenAI’s Affirmative Action and Equal Employment Opportunity Policy Statement . Background checks for applicants will be administered in accordance with applicable law, and qualified applicants with arrest or conviction records will be considered for employment consistent with those laws, including the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance for Employers, and the California Fair Chance Act, for US-based candidates. For unincorporated Los Angeles County workers: we reasonably believe that criminal history may have a direct, adverse and negative relationship with the following job duties, potentially resulting in the withdrawal of a conditional offer of employment: protect computer hardware entrusted to you from theft, loss or damage; return all computer hardware in your possession (including the data contained therein) upon termination of employment or end of assignment; and maintain the confidentiality of proprietary, confidential, and non-public information. In addition, job duties require access to secure and protected information technology systems and related data security obligations. To notify OpenAI that you believe this job posting is non-compliant, please submit a report through this form . No response will be provided to inquiries unrelated to job posting compliance. We are committed to providing reasonable accommodations to applicants with disabilities, and requests can be made via this link . OpenAI Global Applicant Privacy Policy At OpenAI, we believe artificial intelligence has the potential to help people solve immense global challenges, and we want the upside of AI to be widely shared. Join us in shaping the future of technology.

descriptionAr: About Ramp Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $275B in annualized spend flows in and out of 85,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books. The problems are high-stakes, data-dense, and unforgiving. We hire people with high agency and high urgency. We look for slope over intercept. We care less about where you trained and more about what you’ve built. At Ramp, everyone is a builder who owns problems end to end and makes consequential decisions that shape the outcome. The median Ramp customer saves 7.5% and grows revenue 16% in their first year – far in excess of businesses operating without Ramp. We believe every ambitious company deserves the same. If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it. About the Role Paying vendors is one of the most manual, error-prone jobs in finance. Invoices arrive by email and PDF, get keyed in by hand, wait on approvals, and then have to be paid on time, by the right method, for the right amount, and recorded correctly in the books. A single mistake can mean a late fee, a duplicate payment, or an unhappy vendor. Ramp's Bill Pay team builds the accounts payable system that automates that work end to end: bill intake and parsing, approvals, payment execution by ACH, check, card, and international transfer, vendor credits, and sync to customers' accounting systems. Bill Pay is one of Ramp's fastest-growing products, and businesses rely on it every day to move large amounts of money. We're looking for a senior backend engineer to own a core part of that system. You'll take responsibility for an area such as payment execution, bill intake and AI-powered extraction, approvals, or accounting sync, set its technical direction within the team, and keep it correct and reliable as volume grows. You'll work closely with product, design, and payments partners to make accounts payable faster and more trustworthy for finance teams. What You'll Do Own the design and evolution of a core Bill Pay system, such as payment execution, bill intake, approvals, or accounting sync, from technical design through launch, monitoring, and iteration Build payment workflows that move money correctly across ACH, check, card, and international rails, with strong safeguards against duplicate, late, or incorrect payments Build AI-powered AP automation, including invoice extraction, auto-coding, and agents that reduce manual review for finance teams Design data models that keep every bill, approval, payment, and credit accurate and traceable through to the general ledger Build reliable integrations with ERPs and accounting systems that stay consistent through retries, partial failures, and edits on either side Improve the reliability, performance, and observability of Bill Pay systems as customers process larger payment volumes Drive technical direction for your area and raise the engineering bar through design reviews, code reviews, and mentorship What You'll Need Experience designing, building, and operating production backend systems, including APIs, data models, and asynchronous workflows A track record of owning a system or product area end to end and shaping its technical direction over time Strong system design judgment, especially around correctness, idempotency, and reliability in systems where mistakes have real financial impact Product sense: you care about the customer problem, not just the ticket, and you balance speed with quality Clear communication and a collaborative approach to technical decisions across product, design, and engineering Nice to Haves Experience with accounts payable, payments, money movement, or other financial systems Experience building integrations with ERPs or accounting systems, such as NetSuite or QuickBooks Experience applying LLMs, OCR, or other automation to document processing or financial workflows Experience scaling high-volume, event-driven You'll maintain a consistent global core while tailoring examples, facilitation, sequencing, and practice to the market. You'll partner with Sales Leadership, Revenue Operations, Product Marketing, onboarding teams, and frontline managers to equip the field with the skills, workflows, and just-in-time guidance to execute our GTM strategy. Review results regularly, distinguish correlation from causation, and recommend corrective action when adoption or performance is off track Lead cross-functional initiatives to align product releases, go-to-market strategies, and enablement rollouts Partner with onboarding teams to reinforce role-based ramp milestones through hands-on application, practice, and proficiency checks Build technical and workflow fluency programs that help the field uncover customer needs, translate business problems into practical Notion workflows, and demonstrate their value Activate frontline managers first with previews, toolkits, coaching prompts, and consistent reinforcement and inspection cadences AMER activation & regional adaptation Collaborate with regional segment leads to proactively identify segment & market dynamics, competitive landscapes, and customer behavior patterns Adapt global programs to address regional needs while maintaining core methodology and brand consistency Create region-specific content, case studies, and competitive battle cards that resonate with local markets Build feedback loops between regional teams and global program development to continuously improve our approach Partner with regional managers to coach, inspect, and reinforce priority behaviors in existing team cadences; use field feedback to improve adoption and program design Skills You'll Need to Bring: Experience & Expertise 7-10+ years of experience in sales enablement, revenue operations, or similar go-to-market roles Proven track record of building and scaling enablement programs across multiple geographies, with a consistent global core and effective regional adaptation Expertise in adult learning methodologies and designing multimodal experiences that build and assess proficiency through practice, application, and reinforcement High proficiency with the enablement tool stack including emerging AI and automation solutions (ideally AI is already embedded into your workflow) Experience working with global sales teams and understanding of diverse market dynamics Strong analytical skills and experience defining target behaviors, tracking leading indicators and business outcomes, and improving programs based on evidence Skills & Qualities Demonstrate ability to build and automate Enablement and field work through AI workflows Strategic thinker who can balance global consistency with local relevance Excellent communication and presentation skills, comfortable working with senior leadership Natural collaborator who thrives in cross-functional environments Data-driven approach to decision making with strong attention to detail Adaptable and comfortable with ambiguity in a fast-growing environment Passionate about developing people and helping teams reach their potential Technical Requirements Proficiency with AI tools for workflow development, gamification, content creation, data analysis, and process automation Strong project management skill

descriptionAr: Grafana Labs is the company behind Grafana Cloud, the fully managed observability platform trusted by more than 10,000 organizations to ensure reliability, resolve incidents faster, and optimize telemetry at scale. Built on open source and open standards and designed for interoperability across any stack, Grafana Cloud brings AI to observability and observability to AI, giving teams (and their agents) unified visibility so they can see, understand, and act on all their disparate data, wherever it lives, and move at the speed of their ambitions. Customers, including Anthropic, Bloomberg, NVIDIA, Microsoft, and Salesforce, rely on Grafana Labs. We are a 100% remote company with team members across 40+ countries, backed by leading investors including Lightspeed Venture Partners, Sequoia Capital, GIC, Coatue, J.P. Morgan, CapitalG, and Lead Edge Capital. Learn more at grafana.com and follow us on LinkedIn and X . We’re scaling fast and staying true to what makes us different: an open-source legacy, a global collaborative culture, and a passion for meaningful work. Our team thrives in an innovation-driven environment where transparency, autonomy, and trust fuel everything we do. You may not meet every requirement, and that’s okay. If this role excites you, we’d love you to raise your hand for what could be a truly career-defining opportunity. The Opportunity: Product Marketing at Grafana Labs lives in the Product org, not the Marketing org, and we think differently about the job. As Grafana's offering shifts from dashboards to observability agents, our team closes the gap between what our products can do and how customers understand that value. We build clear, consistent positioning, run marketing campaigns that attract new customers, and create content that helps engineering teams see why Grafana Cloud is the right choice for them. Rather than only executing launches and campaigns, we teach Grafana’s product managers and engineers how to think about growth and demand. We also codify product marketing knowledge into AI-forward tools and processes that anyone at Grafana can use. For example, we all contribute product information to a shared knowledge base, which we use to generate enablement materials and decks. The Operations Manager keeps the Product Marketing system running and makes it better. You'll track how our work performs and report on it to the team every week, experiment with new AI workflows, and maintain the collateral and tools the team and the field depend on, so the sales team is fully supported in positioning our products. You'll work closely with the team's software engineers: you test ideas like sales deck generators or tools for competitive analysis, script prototypes, and define what good output looks like, and they turn the best ideas into production tools. You'll also coordinate with the field, Enablement, and Marketing so we understand each other's goals and make progress on shared initiatives. For this role you don't need to be a product marketer but you should have experience working inside a Product or Marketing organization for a software company. Since we don’t have an operations manager yet, you’ll also help to shape your own role. You should arrive with a desire to find and solve imperfectly-defined problems. What You'll Be Doing: Projects and Cross-Functional Initiatives : Drive cross-functional initiatives that align with product marketing strategies across GTM, Product, and Marketing teams. Own follow-ups, task tracking, and on-time completion. Cross-Team Coordination : Coordinate with the field, Enablement, and Marketing teams so we understand each other's goals and priorities. Track shared initiatives, and coordinate enablement activities with the Enablement team. Analytics and Reporting : Track the product marketing team's key metrics, such as how our content, enablement sessions, and launches perform and who uses them. Interpret and report on them to the team every week. AI Experimentation and Prototyping : Try out new AI workflows and tools, using AI to write scripts and checking that they work. Decide what good output looks like and codify that judgment in evaluations, working alongside the software engineers on our team as they refine and deploy tools. Hand the most promising prototypes to engineers to make production-ready. For example, you might test a deck generator with sellers, write evals for it, and communicate about it internally. Collateral Management : Maintain the team's most important collateral, including core decks, positioning content, and enablement sessions. Keep it accurate and current, share it widely, and make sure sellers know where to find it and how to use it. Knowledge Base Stewardship : Help keep our shared product knowledge base complete and current. Spot missing or stale information, chase down the owners, and improve the processes that keep it up to date. What Makes You a Great Fit: 2+ years in an operations, analytics, enablement, or technical support role within a Product or Marketing organization for a software company. Strong analytical judgment: you use AI and other tools to pull data, check the results instead of taking them at face value, and turn the numbers into clear recommendations Proficiency with AI agents, including building skills and automated workflows that more than one person uses Good judgment about what makes AI output good, and the ability to codify that judgment in evaluations Ability to quickly understand our products and describe their value: what SREs and platform engineers do, and how observability products help them Ability to build dashboards and pages in Grafana, or to learn quickly Strong project management and organizational skills Excellent verbal and written communication skills, including presenting data to a team Bonus Points For: Strong bias to action: you build, test, and ship instead of waiting for permission Able to manage multiple projects and priorities at once Adaptable, flexible, a
