When a customer's problem needs more than a best-practices doc, such as a custom integration, a tricky instrumentation setup, or a working prototype, you'll build it with them, then turn what you learn into repeatable patterns for the rest of the team. Forward deployed work is new here and you will have a part in building this arm. You'll start with the core Solutions Engineering work and take on more hands-on deployment work as customers pull you into it, helping define what this motion looks like at Sentry. The goal is simple: reduce time to value. The outcomes we care about: Developers can quickly find and resolve slowdowns and errors in their applications. Get Sentry set up, in the code. With the customer's permission, work in their codebase like a member of their engineering team, delivering the pull requests that fully set up Sentry so data is flowing from day one. Instrument what matters most. Add custom telemetry for a customer's most critical user journeys and build the dashboards and alerts that go with it. Lead migrations. Move customers off their existing observability tools by setting up their Sentry organization and delivering PRs that introduce Sentry and remove the old solution. Work like a trusted contractor. Stay within the scope and access you've been given, take extra care in live environments, test thoroughly, and ship pull requests that customer engineers are glad to merge. Embed with their teams, including on site, when it helps. Build the motion. Turn one-off deployments into repeatable playbooks and tooling, help define how forward deployed engagements are scoped and measured, and bring what you learn back to Product and Engineering. About the Role As Strategy and Operations lead, you will develop country strategies, identify the most important market opportunities and barriers, align cross-functional teams around a focused set of priorities, and personally drive initiatives through to measurable outcomes. This is an individual-contributor role. The primary focus is Consumer, with opportunities to create adjacent impact across B2B. You will go deep in a small number of priority markets while building approaches that can scale across EMEA. This is not a strategy-only role. The successful candidate will combine rigorous analysis and market judgment with urgency, hands-on execution and the ability to influence without formal authority. This role is based in Munich or Berlin. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees. In this role, you will: Build country strategies: Develop plans, priorities and forecasts for key European markets and translate company strategy into practical local action. descriptionAr: Mid-Market Implementation Specialist (German Speaking) Hi! I'm Daryl, and I'm the Manager of High Touch (Mid-Market) Implementations at Ashby. The Ashby team has grown rapidly over the last few years, and we're not slowing down: we added more than 2,100 new customers in the last year alone and now support over 5,000 customers, with ARR growing much faster than 100% year over year. We're expecting similarly fast growth this year, and every one of those new customers needs a thoughtful implementation to actually get value out of Ashby. We'll share more details once we meet, but you probably have a good idea as to why we're expanding this team! The Role: We're looking for a Mid-Market Implementation Specialist who excels at leading technically complex, hands on implementation projects for B2B SaaS customers. You'll own each implementation from the moment Sales hands it off through go-live; part project manager, part technical expert, and part trusted advisor to the customer! Six months in, success looks like carrying a full book of 15-20 active implementations, running each customer relationship on your own (kickoff, timeline, follow-through), independently solving complex configuration and workflow challenges, and handling the normal bumps (a slow-to-respond customer, a technical snag, an escalation) without the rest of your book slipping. Guide teams in designing and implementing AI-enhanced development workflows, agentic systems, automations, evaluations, and scalable application architectures. descriptionAr: About Ramp Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $275B in annualized spend flows in and out of 85,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books. The problems are high-stakes, data-dense, and unforgiving. We hire people with high agency and high urgency. We look for slope over intercept. We care less about where you trained and more about what you’ve built. At Ramp, everyone is a builder who owns problems end to end and makes consequential decisions that shape the outcome. The median Ramp customer saves 7.5% and grows revenue 16% in their first year – far in excess of businesses operating without Ramp. We believe every ambitious company deserves the same. If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it. About the Role Ramp is, at its core, a fintech company. Our financial infrastructure enables us to issue cards, move money globally, and manage treasury flows for our customers. Stablecoins are emerging as a critical lever to make these flows faster, cheaper, and more accessible. We are looking for a Software Engineer to join our engineering team with a dedicated focus on stablecoin-based payment and treasury systems. In this role, you will act as both a technical owner and multiplier: working on core stablecoin services, ensuring secure and reliable integrations with external partners, and guiding Ramp’s evolution toward next-generation fintech solutions. Our ideal candidate combines deep curiosity about eventually consistent distributed systems with strong financial infrastructure experience, thrives in highly regulated and mission-critical environments, and has a passion for diving into new problem spaces. What You'll Do Help build & scale Ramp’s stablecoin-based payment and treasury infrastructure Partner with external providers and internal stakeholders to deliver end-to-end product flows Solve Ramp’s toughest fintech challenges with new technologies Collaborate with engineers across Ramp to integrate stablecoin capabilities into core products What You Need Minimum 5+ years of experience shipping high-quality architectures for critical systems preferred Proven experience with stablecoin technologies, blockchain-based payment rails, and/or wallet infrastructure Strong production experience with cloud environments (AWS, GCP, or Azure) and Infrastructure-as-Code (Terraform or equivalent) Deep proficiency in at least one object-oriented or functional programming language (Python, Go, Java, or similar) Experience working on security-sensitive systems, with interest in key management, wallet security, or secure transaction flows. Experience building or operating payments, money movement, treasury, stablecoin, or crypto infrastructure in production environments Nice to Have Intuition for on-chain UX and settlement mechanics, including wallet-based transaction signing, confirmation/finality, and chain-level tradeoffs like fees and latency. Direct experience building on-chain wallets or with integrating a crypto onramp / offramp APIs for custody and remittance flows Experience integrating with external financial service providers and APIs at scale Familiarity with cross-border settlement, FX, or treasury management systems Background in highly regulated fintech environments (e.g., payments, banking, or government-compliant infrastructure) Benefits available to all full-time Ramp employees (Global) Flexible PTO Centralized home-office equipment ordering Health and wellness stipend Budget for intra-office travel Weekly coffee stipend United States 100% medical, dental & vision insurance coverage for you, with partial coverage for dependents One Medical annual membership 401(k), including employer match on contributions made while employed by Ramp Fertility HRA (up to $10,000 per year) Parental leave: up to 16 weeks (birthing + bonding) or 8 weeks (bonding only) at 100% pay Pet insurance In-office perks: lunch, snacks, drinks, and more Relocation expense coverage to NYC or SF (if needed) Canada Group medical, dental, and vision coverage through Sun Life Life, AD&D, and disability coverage Fertility drug coverage (up to $4,000 lifetime) Group Retirement Plan with employer match (RRSP + DPSP) Parental leave: up to 16 weeks (birthing + bonding) or 8 weeks (bonding only) at 100% pay, with additional time available at reduced pay Employee Assistance Program and virtual care through Lumino Health United Kingdom Private medical insurance through Freedom Elite Virtual GP and at-home care via eMed x Livi Workplace pension through Penfold, with salary sacrifice option Parental leave: up to 16 weeks (birthing + bonding) or 8 weeks (bonding only) at 100% pay with additional time available at reduced pay Referral Instructions If you are being referred for the role, please contact that person to apply on your behalf. Other notices Pursuant to the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, we will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records. Beware of recruiting scams: Ramp will only contact you through official @ Ramp.com email addresses and will never ask for payment or sensitive personal information during the hiring process. Our teams are building the full Super Intelligence stack: from our Colossus supercomputers, to Grok models, to our suite of applications, including Grok Bot, Grok Build, Grok Imagine, Grok Voice, and X. This is a deeply technical, post-sale role embedded inside SpaceXSI's most strategic enterprise accounts. Solution Architects sit at the center of long-term customer transformation. RESPONSIBILITIES: Help Engineering Teams Adopt AI-Native Development: Roll out SpaceXSI across strategic engineering organizations; configure environments, design workflows, and run hands-on enablement sessions; help developers integrate SpaceXSI into real production workflows, not isolated demos; drive fast time-to-value and durable adoption across teams; identify workflow friction and solve problems quickly Expand SpaceXSI Across the Organization: Identify where SpaceXSI should expand next inside the customer environment; help engineering organizations evolve from isolated usage to company-wide adoption; design rollout strategies for new workflows, teams, and platform groups; partner with customers to operationalize AI-assisted development at scale; work closely with Account Executives during major expansion moments Become a Trusted Technical Partner: Build deep relationships with developers, platform teams, engineering leadership, and executive stakeholders; lead architecture reviews, technical working sessions, and strategic planning discussions; advise customers on developer productivity, workflow design, governance, and AI adoption strategy; coordinate across Sales, Product, Engineering, and Customer Success to unblock customer progress; help organizations navigate workflow and operational change as AI-native development evolves Drive Real Customer Outcomes: Help customers translate adoption into measurable engineering impact; connect SpaceXSI usage to outcomes like faster iteration cycles, improved developer productivity, workflow efficiency, and engineering quality; help customers communicate the value of SpaceXSI internally and build momentum for broader adoption; turn successful deployments into repeatable workflow patterns across the organization Help Make SpaceXSI Indispensable: Deepen workflow adoption and long-term product stickiness; monitor competitive risk and help customers standardize on SpaceXSI over time; support recovery plans when adoption slows or competing tools gain traction; help customers build workflows they can't imagine operating without Shape the Future of the Product: Bring structured feedback from strategic customers into Product and Engineering; identify emerging workflow patterns, friction points, and enterprise requirements; help shape new capabilities through lighthouse customers and design partnerships; turn successful customer workflows into reusable playbooks and reference patterns BASIC QUALIFICATIONS: Technical background in software engineering, infrastructure, DevOps, platform engineering, or developer tooling Experience in a customer-facing technical role such as Solutions Architect, Solutions Engineer, Forward Deployed Engineer, Technical Account Manager, Enterprise Architect, or similar PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE: The ability to work hands-on with engineering teams while also operating strategically with technical leadership A strong understanding of developer workflows, SDLC tooling, integrations, CI/CD systems, governance, and enterprise engineering environments Excellent communication skills and the ability to explain complex technical concepts clearly across both technical and executive audiences Strong instincts around workflow design, adoption strategy, and driving workflow change across engineering teams High ownership, strong execution skills, and comfort operating in fast-moving environments with ambiguity A passion for developer tooling and strong conviction around how AI will reshape software engineering ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS: Remote role (United States) Must be willing to travel 40-50% COMPENSATION AND BENEFITS: The expected annual base salary range for this role is $164,500 - $210,000. This role is also eligible for sales commissions or bonuses, with an annual on-target earnings (OTE) range of $235,000 - $300,000. OTE includes base salary plus target incentive compensation, assuming 100% achievement of applicable performance targets. Actual incentive earnings depend on performance and the terms of the applicable plan. Your actual level and base salary will be determined on a case-by-case basis and may vary based on the following considerations: job-related knowledge and skills, education, and experience. Base salary is just one part of our total rewards package at SpaceXSI, which also includes equity, comprehensive medical, vision, and dental coverage, access to a 401(k) retirement plan, short & long-term disability insurance, life insurance, and various other discounts and perks.

descriptionAr: Hi 👋 I'm Harriet, and I lead Marketing at Ashby. We've built a business with 5,500+ customers, a highly differentiated product, and a brand that people genuinely care about. We've invested in content, customer stories, community, and the foundations of a strong marketing program. Now, we have an opportunity to build a much bigger paid engine to support our next stage of growth. We're looking for a Senior Paid Marketing Manager to build it. You'll take ownership of our existing LinkedIn program and expand across Meta, Google Search, YouTube, and other channels. You'll have meaningful budget, strong creative and technical partners, and the autonomy to build a program that creates qualified pipeline and strengthens our brand. This is a hands-on role. We want someone who knows their channels inside out, enjoys getting into the details, and can take a campaign from initial hypothesis through execution, analysis, and optimization. You'll have access to specialist support when it makes sense, but you'll be the person driving the work. We also believe AI creates an opportunity for exceptional individual contributors to do work that previously required much larger teams. We're looking for someone who is already exploring that opportunity and wants to push it further. What makes this role interesting You get to build with the resources most marketers wish they had. Paid is relatively underdeveloped at Ashby compared with the scale of our business. You get to build something substantial without unwinding years of accumulated complexity or fighting for the resources to make it work. We have strong content, customer proof, product differentiation, and an established brand. You'll start with a monthly budget in the hundreds of thousands of dollars and the support of our design, web, and RevOps teams. You can rethink how paid marketing gets done. We want to enable exceptional individual contributors to accomplish more through AI, automation, and better workflows. You'll have the freedom to experiment with new tools, build systems that improve your output, and challenge established ways of working. You'll build a program that makes the brand and business stronger. We believe great paid marketing combines analytical rigor with creative judgment. You'll optimize for pipeline and efficiency while building campaigns that earn attention, communicate our differentiation, and give the right buyers a reason to care about Ashby. We don't want a lead-generation machine that makes our brand worse. What you'll own Build and scale our paid program. Own strategy and execution across LinkedIn, Meta, and Google Search, expanding into YouTube and other channels as opportunities emerge. Prioritize audiences, develop campaign hypotheses, manage budgets, and turn promising experiments into repeatable sources of qualified pipeline. Drive creative strategy and experimentation. Develop campaign concepts, write ad copy, brief creative, and shape landing-page tests. Work closely with design, content, and product marketing to produce distinctive work. Build a disciplined testing cadence across audiences, creative, offers, and conversion paths, knowing when to scale, iterate, or stop. Use AI to increase your impact. Build practical workflows using AI, agents, and automation to improve research, creative iteration, campaign operations, and analysis. We want someone who actively experiments with new approaches, evaluates their effectiveness, and turns what works into repeatable systems. Own measurement and performance. Drive our approach to paid measurement in partnership with RevOps. Establish the signals and reporting needed to understand qualified reach, conversion, pipeline contribution, and efficiency. Develop better ways to assess incrementality, make informed decisions with imperfect attribution, and translate performance data into clear investment recommendations. Connect campaigns to the buyer journey. Partner with sales, lifecycle, and ABM to understand what makes an opportunity valuable and how paid can influence the journey from first touch through pipeline. Adapt messaging and investment to our customer segments and markets. What you'll work on in your first six months Take ownership of LinkedIn, identifying opportunities to improve qualified reach, creative, and progression into pipeline. Build and scale Meta, establishing a strong creative testing cadence and the landing pages and follow-up needed to make the channel work. Expand Google Search and launch YouTube, evaluating additional channels where there's a compelling audience and learning opportunity. Establish a stronger operating system for paid, including AI-enabled workflows, measurement, and a clear approach to allocating investment. The goal isn't to scale every channel equally. It's to build a broad set of opportunities, learn quickly, and concentrate investment where the evidence is strongest. What we're looking for We care more about what you've built and how you think than the number of years you've spent in marketing. You're a domain expert in paid media. You have deep, hands-on expertise in LinkedIn, Meta, and Google Ads. You understand the platforms, know how to structure and optimize campaigns, and can explain how your decisions have influenced qualified pipeline. You've personally built and scaled programs in sales-led B2B SaaS. You're a builder, not just a strategist. You're excited to get into the accounts, develop the creative, run experiments, investigate performance, and solve problems yourself. You know when external expertise can help, but you don't need an agency to do the core work. You combine analytical rigor with creative taste. You understand performance metrics and experimentation, but you also know what makes advertising compelling. You can connect campaign decisions to buyer quality and pipeline without losing sight of the brand you're building. You're already changing how you work with AI. You can demonstrate how you've used AI too

An overview of this role The Pipeline Authoring group develops tools for creating and managing your pipelines. We balance maintaining core functionality of the product with developing newer areas. Our key areas of focus are CI/CD components and the CI/CD Catalog , which allows users to discover, reuse, and contribute CI/CD components to make software development more efficient and productive. As a Backend Engineer, you will work on maturing our Catalog and Component functionality and reliability, improve and maintain performance, scalability and security of Pipeline Creation, and always consider usability and user experience in these key areas of the product. Your contributions and collaboration with your fellow team members will ensure that GitLab CI/CD remains a best in class solution. Some of the things we have recently been working on include: Inputs for Pipelines Inputs for Jobs Inputs Enhancements CI/CD Catalog - UX improvements Learn more on the Pipeline Authoring direction pages: Pipeline Composition   Component Catalog   About the team The Pipeline Authoring team is made up of experienced Engineers, some having worked in this area for many years and some having joined more recently. The team shares a passion for finding solutions to complex challenges that scale and are maintainable. Located across five countries and several time zones, async communication is key to our success. The team lives by GitLab’s core values and is always eager to improve. Many things in GitLab begin with a pipeline, so our team regularly interacts with other GitLab teams, community contributors and customers as we strive to create the best possible Pipeline Authoring experience. Learn more on the Pipeline Authoring group handbook page and Pipeline Authoring Unfiltered playlist . Ship small features and improvements with minimal guidance and support from other team members. Collaborate with the team on larger projects. Advocate for improvements to reliability, security, and performance. Recognize impediments to our efficiency as a team (“technical debt”), propose and implement solutions. Participate in agile development practices, including async planning sessions, stand-ups, and retrospectives, to drive iterative software development and continuous improvement for the team. Contribute to our development process by asking questions and providing feedback to make us better as a team. Embrace continuous learning and stay connected with industry best practices, tools, and technologies to drive improvements in our software. Participate in Tier 2 on-call rotations to assist troubleshooting product operations, security operations, and urgent engineering issues. Sales roles are also eligible for incentive pay targeted at up to 100% of the offered base salary. Grade level and salary ranges are determined through interviews and a review of education, experience, knowledge, skills, abilities of the applicant, equity with other team members, alignment with market data, and geographic location and having regard to any applicable collective agreements. descriptionAr: About the Team The Intelligence and Investigations team is dedicated to ensuring the safe, responsible deployment of AI by rapidly detecting and mitigating abuse. Our team leverages cutting-edge testing methodologies to uncover vulnerabilities and emerging threats, helping safeguard OpenAI’s products and users. We work closely with cross-functional partners across product, policy, and engineering to drive a comprehensive defense strategy against evolving adversarial challenges. About the Role As a Novel Abuse Red Teamer, you’ll advance our pre- and post-deployment testing efforts at OpenAI, ensuring our models and products remain resilient against evolving, real-world adversarial threats. We are seeking a self-starter to design, execute, and refine innovative adversarial testing and simulation protocols that leverage state-of-the-art tools and a hands-on red team approach. In this role, you will simulate threat actor methodologies and conduct rigorous application testing to uncover novel abuse vectors. You will serve as a critical technical bridge between our security, product, and policy teams by employing an attacker mindset and advanced red team tactics to drive actionable insights that strengthen our detection mechanisms and overall product defenses. The ideal candidate will have a strong background in application security or penetration testing, with hands-on experience in web application security and proficiency in tools such as Burp Suite, Metasploit, and similar. We value professionals with excellent communication skills, a commitment to continuous learning, and a passion for securing AI technologies through innovative testing methodologies. This role is based in San Francisco, CA. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees. In this role, you will: Design and execute high-fidelity, realistic attack simulations that emulate sophisticated threat actor methodologies, uncovering hidden exploitation vectors through advanced red teaming and application testing techniques. Analyze testing outcomes and generate actionable insights to refine our detection mechanisms, ultimately bolstering our overall security posture. Serve as a crucial technical bridge between our security, product, and policy teams, ensuring that insights from adversarial testing inform broader defense strategies and remediation efforts. Develop and integrate automation tools to streamline testing workflows and enable rapid iteration in response to emerging threats. Collaborate closely with internal stakeholders to align testing strategies with evolving product needs and security objectives. You might thrive in this role if you have / are: Experience in application security, penetration testing, or red team operations, with a proven track record of executing adversarial testing and simulation protocols. A strong technical background in web application security, coupled with hands-on expertise performing security testing of web applications, AI systems, and highly unique attack surfaces. An attacker mindset and a passion for identifying novel abuse vectors in live environments, along with the ability to translate complex technical findings into actionable insights. Demonstrated success in working cross-functionally within fast-paced, dynamic environments, managing complex product ecosystems, and driving rapid security enhancements. Committed to continuous learning, innovation, and the pursuit of cutting-edge security methodologies to protect and advance AI technologies. FORWARD DEPLOYED ENGINEER - WESTERN EUROPE You embed directly with customer teams as the engineer on the ground: own an outcome, ship a production-grade SpaceXSI system that still runs after you leave, and become the critical technical feedback loop from the field back to product engineering. The work is the project. One week you might take a messy business workflow and put a production agent on it: pick the use case, stand up the architecture, wire it into the customer's auth, data, and tools, then harden it with evals until the team actually uses it. Another week you might live in a customer's repo and delivery system and ship an agent-powered path for a migration, a PR review loop, or an incident-to-fix flow, behind tests, review, and rollout rather than in a chat sidebar. RESPONSIBILITIES: Lead discovery with the customer: orient in their codebases and workflows, find the real bottleneck and the use case worth building, and define clear success metrics Design and ship production agents, AI applications, and coding-agent workflows on Grok and our models, on live business processes and inside the customer’s engineering org Get a first version live in days, then harden it over weeks with rollout, monitoring, and iteration from real usage Own production quality: tracing, evals, debugging model or delivery failures, and latency and cost tradeoffs Build the systems around the model (tools, MCP servers, retrieval, rules, skills, CI gates, and evals) and integrate them into the customer’s auth, data, workflow, and delivery systems; decide when prompting, architecture, data, process, or a model change is the right lever Measure the outcome that matters (revenue, cost, hours saved, error rate, cycle time, escaped defects), not seat adoption Work directly with Staff+, platform, and domain leaders, going deep in their systems while communicating clearly about tradeoffs and results Leave the customer team able to run what you built, and turn what you learn into reusable patterns and improvements to SpaceXSI products BASIC QUALIFICATIONS: You have 5+ years of experience in software engineering, machine learning engineering, or data science You’ve owned a customer or operator outcome, not just a slide or a prototype, and can turn a fuzzy problem into a scoped, shipped system You’ve built and owned AI-native workflows or agents in production (using Python, JavaScript/TypeScript), and debugged real production failures (model, tool, data, pipeline, or delivery path) PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE: 2+ years in a customer-facing role, leading discovery conversations and being accountable for outcomes for external stakeholders Hands-on depth in several of: agents and tool-calling, eval harnesses, retrieval and context systems, CI/CD or developer platforms, and AI-native coding workflows in a real repo Experience as a forward-deployed, solutions, or platform engineer embedded with customers, or as a founding engineer who owned an AI product end to end
